newsitem.title: USA: Daytime curfew aimed at Oregon skateboarders.
newsitem.headline: Daytime curfew aimed at Oregon skateboarders.

text.p: The Salem City Council has approved an experimental daytime curfew on students to take effect with the next school year.

While many cities have established nighttime curfews for juveniles in an effort to curb gangs and crimimanl activity, Monday night's measure in Oregon's capital city is unusual because it restricts student movements day and night.

Under the measure, which was sparked by concern about heavy schooltime use of a new downtown municipal skateboard park, police can pick up juveniles under 18 who cannot show an excuse for being on the streets instead of in school, city recorder Jean Lay said.
Home-school and private-school students will need special identification allowing them to be out during public-school class hours.
The curfew will automatically expire in June 1998 unless it is renewed after a public hearing.
The ordinance also establishes a nighttime curfew of 10 p.m. for those under 16 and midnight for 16- and 17-year-olds.
